::: {.recap}
**Where we are.** Linear Q is limited and naive neural Q is unstable. This module asks one question: *Which changes make neural Q-learning stable, and what bias remains?*
:::

## What you will build {#build}

In this module you will:

- Implement a replay buffer and explain the two problems it fixes.
- Implement DQN with a target network and the Huber loss, masking only on terminated.
- Derive the max-of-noisy-estimates bias, implement Double DQN and measure Q against Monte Carlo returns.
- Place your live seed against recorded bands of the reference DQN and SB3's DQN at the same budget.

## Before you start {#before}

- [Module 7 · Function approximation and why it can diverge](/modules/07-function-approximation.qmd) and its lab: this module builds on what it left open.
- A Google account (Colab's default CPU runtime is enough), or a local or AWS setup from the [Setup page](/setup.qmd).
- No API keys or paid services.
